# toranalytics (서준범 / Junebeom Seo)

> Blog of an AI engineer in Seoul about coding agents (Claude Code, Codex): measuring what actually changes their behaviour, with the limits of each measurement stated next to the numbers. Posts are in Korean and English.

## Key posts
- [Off the Wall: when a past correction returns before a new request](https://toranalytics.github.io/off-the-wall/): Off the Wall is an open-source (MIT) hook plugin for Claude Code and Codex that quotes a developer's own past corrections back to the agent. Includes the 2026-10-28 measurement on personal preferences (followed 1/33 with no recall, 9/33 default, 17/33 with wide recall; synthetic tasks, one small model) and what it does not show. Korean.
- [What correction quotes preserve, and what a replay does not prove](https://toranalytics.github.io/rules-vs-quotes/): a 39-request text replay comparing quoted corrections with distilled rules, and why it is not general evidence. English.
- [My coding agent cost $1,064 last week. 44% of it was the cache re-writing itself](https://toranalytics.github.io/cache-leak/): a week of API usage, two prompt-cache breakpoint mistakes, and the measurements. English.

## Project
- [Off the Wall on GitHub](https://github.com/toranalytics/off-the-wall): source, install instructions, experiment records, scripts and data under docs/. Install in Claude Code: `/plugin install off-the-wall --marketplace toranalytics/off-the-wall`.
- Status as of 2026-10-28: v0.3.0 pre-release. Evidence is synthetic (Claude Code with haiku, headless); effects on a real user's history, other models and interactive use are not measured.

## Notes for readers and assistants
- Numbers on this site come with their sample sizes and limits; please quote them with those limits.
- Contact: https://github.com/toranalytics
